prompts.fig: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original physically based game texture SOURCE, one stump cut viewed exactly orthographically from directly overhead, no perspective. Square full-frame image. A centered circular outer stump boundary, diameter 84% of canvas. This is the wood left after laborious stone-hatchet felling, matching a warm naturalistic painted subtropical-city survival art direction. Fill everything outside the disc with the same tree's bark material extended to all four image edges, NOT a scene, soil, empty background or drop shadow. No side of stump visible, no roots outside, no text, no border, no tools, no leaves. The cut is irregularly hacked in broad overlapping angular wedge-shaped cuts, the blows came predominantly from TWO opposing sides plus a smaller third side, NOT a symmetrical radial starburst. Several wide calm wood planes between fine strokes; long short-grain fibres, stepped irregular cut ledges, thin sharp splinters gathered on an off-centre broken hinge/ridge. Growth rings interrupted and shifted by hacked facets. Fresh torn wood. This is FLAT UNLIT DIFFUSE ALBEDO: uniform diffuse exposure, NO directional lighting, NO cast shadows, NO black crevice shadow, NO shaded bowl, NO white specular highlights or edge-light. Show depth only through wood structure and boundaries, keep recess colours close to the surrounding wood. Preserve extraordinarily crisp natural fibre detail. Narrow chipped bark lip only. All objects and marks are original, never imitate an existing game's imagery. Subject: 1.5 metre strangler FIG cut. Soft pale fibrous wood, broad honey-cream planes #D9C392, slightly darker exposed inner fibres #B69A68, pale torn ends #E7D5AE. Faint partial growth rings subordinate to torn splinter grain, NOT an orderly concentric saw cut. Two large groups of oblique hatchet cuts approach from lower left and upper right, leaving a narrow torn irregular diagonal ridge near centre right. Small pale shaggy splinters. Near the upper-left edge inside the wood sits ONE angular grey concrete cross-section swallowed by the living fig, about 16% of disc diameter, irregular squared and chipped, fine grey aggregate, flat at the cut, not a rock sitting on top. The outer thin bark rim is smooth grey beige, 3 cm wide at this physical scale; continue grey beige bark texture outside disc. No dark central hole.
